description: A branching network of twenty-four decay envelopes: one impulse starts the first, and as each envelope falls away it starts the ones connected below it, so a single trigger spreads across the network

params.text: Sets how long each envelope holds before it hands on, which is the delay between one output firing and the ones it feeds
Sets how quickly each envelope falls away once it has fired
Tilts the lag across the network, so later outputs fire at a shorter or longer spacing than the first
Attenuverts the lag CV before it is added to the lag knob
Attenuverts the spread CV before it is added to the spread knob
Attenuverts the decay CV before it is added to the decay knob
Starts an impulse at the first node on each press

inputs.text: A rise past 1V starts an impulse at the first node, and it is ignored while the first output has not yet fallen back below the propagation threshold
Shifts the lag, added to the lag knob through its attenuverter and clamped to a travel of 0.001 to 1
Shifts the decay, added to the decay knob through its attenuverter and clamped to the knob's own travel
Shifts the spread, added to the spread knob through its attenuverter and clamped to the knob's own travel

outputs.text: A decay envelope, 0-10V, which fires when the node feeding it has fallen far enough and then falls away at the decay rate

notes: nothing happens until an impulse arrives, either at the IMPULSE input or from the button beside it; the network then fires once and falls silent
the twenty-four outputs are wired as a fixed branching graph rather than a chain, so one impulse splits into several strands that reach different outputs at different times
the module runs its network at a fixed 44.1kHz rate whatever the engine's sample rate, and interpolates the outputs between those steps
